1.why: Every state-changing endpoint goes through access(), which resolves the account solely from the server-side session's userId (accounts.get(s.userId)) and noId() rejects any client-supplied userId/accountId, so settings always belong to the signed-in user.

2.why: TOTP codes are derived from an account-specific, per-provisioning encrypted secret and recovery codes are hashed per account, so a code valid for one account would not verify for another (only one demo account exists at all).

3.why: Enabling MFA in /api/mfa/verify only sets a.mfa = true and never rotates the current session id nor deletes other sessions from the sessions map, so pre-existing sessions remain valid.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored as AES-GCM ciphertext with a random IV and recovery codes are stored only as salted PBKDF2-SHA256 (210k iterations) hashes.

5.why: Session ids, CSRF tokens, base32 secrets and recovery codes are all generated via crypto.getRandomValues().

6.why: The session cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict and no localStorage/sessionStorage or JS-readable cookie is used; secrets only live transiently in JS variables and the DOM.

7.why: Server validates and normalises email, phone, 6-digit OTP and recovery-code format with strict regexes, caps body size, rejects non-object JSON, and uses in-memory Maps (no SQL string concatenation).

8.why: All dynamic values are injected with textContent (message, logs, setupKey, codeList) and no innerHTML is used, plus a nonce-based CSP without unsafe-inline.

9.why: The application issues no redirects at all and noId() even rejects a 'redirect' field, so no open-redirect path exists, though no explicit allow-list is implemented.

10.why: Responses set nonce-based CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy and Cache-Control: no-store.

11.why: Set-Cookie for mfa_session includes HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict, and logout clears it with the same attributes.

12.why: Error output is generic with no stack traces, but the client explicitly console.logs and writes the live TOTP ('Mock MFA OTP delivered') and all recovery codes into a visible Logs panel, so codes are not kept out of logs.

13.why: Provisioning has a 10-minute expiresAt window, a used flag set after successful verification, TOTP accepts only ±1 30s step, and consumed recovery codes are spliced out of the array.

14.why: wrong()/locked() enforce MAX=5 failures then a 5-minute lockout separately for OTP and recovery codes, and reissue requests are capped at 3 per 10 minutes.

15.why: Sign-in deletes any existing cookie session and issues a fresh random id, sessions enforce 20-min idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and logout deletes the session server-side and clears the cookie; no rotation occurs at the later identity/MFA step.
